title: Shaping Amplitude
concept:
Until now, notes start and stop abruptly the moment you press and release a key. Real instruments do not behave that way — a piano note fades out after you release the key, a bowed string has a slow attack. To control how a note evolves over time, synthesizers use an Envelope.

The ADSR Envelope is the standard envelope shape:

Attack: How long it takes the note to reach full volume after a key is pressed.
Decay: How long it takes to fall from full volume to the Sustain level.
Sustain: The volume level held as long as the key is held down.
Release: How long the note fades out after the key is released.

The Envelope generates a CV signal that rises and falls according to these settings. To use it, you connect the Envelope's output to a VCA (Voltage Controlled Amplifier). The VCA lets the envelope shape the volume of the audio signal passing through it.

The patch already has everything connected except the gate signal: the Keyboard needs to tell the ADSR when a key is pressed. Connect the Keyboard's Gate output to the ADSR's Gate input to activate the envelope.

task.instruction: Connect the Keyboard's gate output to the ADSR's gate input. Click the Keyboard's 'gate' output port (right side), then click the ADSR's 'gate' input port (left side). Then press a key — the note should now fade in and out smoothly.
